notes:
A clean page and one of the better ladders: two evidence points, both checked against the resolver and both the opposite kind to what the header implies. The header's Item Reqs lists 'Demon Pen' and 'Zeelozok's earplug' side by side as if they were the same sort of thing; they are not. Demon Pen is an ordinary item (res/items 1653) that drops off the demons, and Zeelozok's earplug is a key item (res/key_items 634) handed over by the ???. Recording either as the other kind would have cost the quest both of its anchors.

Bullets 5 and 6 are split into three steps -- pop, kill, re-examine -- because bullet 6 explicitly waits on Marquis Andrealphus being defeated, and the earplug only comes from the second examine. The sub-bullets under 5 are all tactics: linking demons, sleepable adds, the Escape trick, and the fact that only the Marquis has to die. None is a step, though the last of them is why the fight step lists only him as a kill and leaves the Bannerets and Secretaries as spawns.

Bullet 4's 'wait 1 earth minute' is a real gate but not a rung of its own -- it is a pause in front of a conversation, so it lives in step 4's note rather than becoming an unmarkable wait step between two steps on the same NPC. The ??? is in OBJECT_DENY and can never carry a marker, so steps 5 and 7 keep their place in the ladder and lose only their pin; the earplug evidence still moves the player on. The Goblin Grenade is the reward and is deliberately not evidence.

notes:
The interesting find here is that 'Frostbloom' resolves as an NPC key but NOT as a key item: res/key_items holds more than one id under that name, and the resolver rejects a non-unique key-item name rather than guess. So the flowers can be MARKED but never OBSERVED. That decides the whole shape of this quest -- the three collection steps carry a real target and no evidence, and the turn-in carries no items list even though the page plainly says you must be holding three, because an unresolvable name in items would buy nothing and could cost the step.

Even if the name did resolve it would be wrong to use: holding one Frostbloom is not holding three, and a single-count evidence on the last group member would jump the ladder to Oruga after the first pick. There is no per-item progress in the packets, so the count stays in the note.

Bullet 3 is three steps, not one and not nine. The page gives three named blooms, each with a primary location and an 'OR' fallback nearby, and says nothing about order -- so they share a group and all three draw at once. The nine 'spawn points' are three spawn points per bloom, not nine separate objectives; that is why the fallbacks are notes rather than rungs. Bullet 2 is the request restated and folds into step 1. The trailing 'Zoning is required in order to repeat' is a cooldown, not a step. Fame 'aule' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing, so region is null and only the raw is kept.

Bullet 4 is routing and becomes a single travel step to Arrapago Reef; the ferry, the North Gate and the Caedarva Mire crossing are one journey to one destination, and the Survival Guide alternative in the sub-bullet is a note. Bullet 5 is the only observable moment: 'Antique automaton' resolves as key item 798, so holding it is what proves the reef trip is done. The two shouted sub-bullets there are worth keeping -- the Corsair ??? is a different one on the same grid reference, and no Lamian Fang Key is needed for this one, which is exactly the sort of thing a player gets wrong.

Bullets 6 and 7 are two conversations with Ghatsad separated by a Vana'diel day. They stay two steps because the page says to speak twice, and nothing unmarkable is wedged between them -- both point at the same NPC in the same place, so the runtime draws one marker either way. The day boundary is not visible to the addon.

Bullet 2 is the one place a verb-scanner would have gone wrong: the sentence names two NPCs, and it is Juroro you speak to -- Ildy-Goldy only appears in the cutscene to hand over the pendulum. notes:
Two randomisations in one three-rung quest, and they are handled differently on purpose. The ITEM is a genuine OR that the schema can express: one of Goblin Bread, Goblin Pie or Goblin Chocolate is asked for, all three are purchasable, all three resolve, so all three sit in items_alt with items left empty -- the shape Cargo, Mandragora-Mad and The Angling Armorer already use for a pure any-one-of-N, rather than promoting one arbitrarily into items. The wiki writes the third as 'Gob. Chocolate Goblin Chocolate' -- the short name and the long name run together by the renderer, both resolving to item 4495 -- and the long name is used as the guide prefers.

The LOCATION cannot be expressed the same way. The Scuff Mark you are sent to is one of three, chosen when you accept the quest, and there is no OR field for places. Rather than pick one grid and be wrong two times in three, or group three rungs that are not an unordered set (you visit exactly one, not all three), the trade step keeps a null grid and lists all three in its note. Scuff Mark resolves as a real NPC key, so a zone-wide, grid-less row still draws on whichever one the client can see -- which is the right behaviour here.

Ramblix (A) appears at the trade but is an NPC and is never fought or spoken to on this page, so he is left out of mobs rather than dressed up as a spawn. Cornelia (A), not the giver, is who completes the quest; the page says so plainly and her grid is taken from bullet 2's own description of Conflux #4. Fame 'agra' is an Abyssea code and gates nothing.

notes:
The page contradicts itself about where it ends: bullet 2 says the second Joachim cutscene completes the quest, and bullet 4 then says to return to Joachim to complete it. Both are recorded in page order and the quest is demoted to medium for it. Bullet 4's own sub-bullet -- 'make sure to get both cutscenes from Joachim' -- is the tell that bullets 1 and 2 really are two separate conversations rather than one restated, so the ladder keeps them apart.

The abyssites are NOT evidence: they are held before each conversation, not granted by it, so they are items on steps 1 and 2. Both resolve as key items (1425 and 1422). What cannot be modelled is the rest of the gate -- four of nine named quests for the first cutscene and five of nine for the second. No packet reports a quest count, so those stay in the notes.

Previous lists 'Heart of Madness' and then three add-on scenario names (The Forbidden Frontier, Scars of Abyssea, Heroes of Abyssea) under an 'Expansion Set Quests' label. Those are not quests and would never resolve as prev titles, so only Heart of Madness is recorded and the rest is flagged. Fame 'Abyssea' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

notes:
Three key items in five bullets, which makes this a well-anchored ladder, but two things keep it at medium.

First, the latent. Bullet 2 says you must break the latent on the Axe of Trials before going any further, and the sub-heading that would have explained how is a transclusion that rendered as an empty line -- the page's own transclusion flag. Breaking it is a long grind with nothing observable and nowhere to stand, so it is not made into a step; a rung the player cannot be tracked through and cannot be marked at is noise. It stays in step 1's note.

Second, the ???. Bullet 3's two sub-bullets put the same object in two places: the northwest corner of (F-6) if you come in by Survival Guide, and (F-5) in the southwest if you Unity Warp to Ro'Maeve and zone across. Both are recorded here; (F-6) is used on the steps because it is the sub-bullet actually giving the spawn instruction.

The evidence split follows the pilot's rule about consumed items. Step 1 grants the Weapon training guide AND the Axe of Trials, but the axe is traded away at step 2, so an AND-list over both would read false the moment you moved on -- only the key item is evidence, and the axe becomes step 2's items requirement instead. Axe of Trials is an ordinary item (16735); the guide, the map and the annals are key items (343, 344, 345).

Bullet 1 is a precondition about other Weapon Skill quests, not a step. 'Great Axe skill 240+' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so the level gate is 71 and jobs stays empty -- great axe is not one job's weapon.

notes:
A short, honest quest. Bullet 2 is not a step -- it is what bullet 1 gives you -- so the Espionage pearlsack (key item 1637) is step 1's evidence, which is exactly where the guide's 'evidence must be obtained AT that step' rule puts it.

Bullet 3's three ??? are one bullet and three steps. They are in one zone, the page states no order between them, and Ferdechiond marks all three on your map at once, so they share a group and draw together; a strict ladder would point at (H-10) and stay silent about the others until you happened to walk to it. Each is a bare ???, which is in OBJECT_DENY and can never carry a marker, so the rungs are kept for their zone and grid and nothing more -- that is still worth having, because the grids are the whole content of the bullet.

Everything under bullet 4 is a reward table: Cruor scales with how fast you finish, timed from accepting the quest to selecting the last ???, not to the hand-in. That is a real mechanic and completely invisible to the addon, so it is a note. The trailing 'Zoning is required to repeat' is a cooldown. Fame 'avun' is an Abyssea code and gates nothing, so only the raw is kept.
